newsitem.title: USA: BPA offers peak firm, non-firm power for Wed.
newsitem.headline: BPA offers peak firm, non-firm power for Wed.

text.p: Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) returned to the next-day peak power market after an absence of nearly a week, the agency said Tuesday.
BPA offered up to 200 megawatts (MW) of firm power for Wednesday at $14.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Northwest deliveries and $15.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
Firm off-peak prices were cut to $10.50 per MWh from $12.50.
Up to 200 MW of non-firm power during hours ending 0800-1000 and 1800-2000 PDT was offered at $15.00 (Northwest) and $16.00 (COB).
Non-firm power during shoulder hours (1100-1700 and 2100-2200 PDT) was offered at $12.00 (Northwest) and $13.00 (COB).
Non-firm power during off-peak hours was offered $10.50 (hours ending 0100-0500 and 2400) and at $11.50 (0600, 2300 PDT) for all deliveries, down $2.00 per MWh from Tuesday prices.
BPA continued to offer displacement power for hours ending 0100-0600 and 2400 PST at $9.00 per MWh and at $7.00 for Northwest buyers only.
